output:
To: t-achilles
Replying to: [p04]
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Achilles sore after upping my k's - rest or push on?

Mel, sounds like a classic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy from the jump in k's rather than a tear. That said, nobody should be diagnosing over the internet, so treat this as general info until someone has actually had a look at it.

On the stretching and injection advice floating around: stretching hard into pain and cortisone injections near the tendon are the two things I'd steer well clear of. Aggressive stretching tends to irritate it further rather than fix it, and steroid injection around the Achilles is associated with weakening the tendon and higher rupture rates. So skipping the needle is the better option here anyway.

The loading that has the best evidence at the moment:
- Heavy slow calf raises, straight knee and bent knee — around 3 sets of 8-12, three times a week, building load slowly. A decent weight beats bodyweight reps off a step.
- Heel drops off a step are fine, but heavy slow calf raises tend to work better.
- Isometric calf holds on the bad days.

Pain monitoring: up to about 3/10 while you're loading it is fine, as long as it's settled by next morning. If it's still sore and no better the following day, you've gone a bit too far — pull the volume or intensity back. I'd keep running, but drop the k's back to what settles easily for now and build from there.

One general thing worth knowing: some antibiotics, particularly the fluoroquinolone family, have been linked with tendon problems and ruptures. If you've had a course of those recently, mention it to your GP.

Get it seen if it's not settling over the next 3-4 weeks — any good sports physio around Bayswater, no need to come to me.

One more thing: stop running and skip the calf work if you get a sudden pop, feel like you've been kicked in the back of the leg, or can't push off properly. That needs checking urgently the same day (GP or ED), because it could be a rupture.
